ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Renate wants to glue together a number of ordinary dice (whose number of points on opposite sides always adds up to 7) to form a "dicebar" as shown. Doing this she only wants to glue sides together with an equal number of points. She wants to make sure that the sum of all points on the non-glued sides equals 2012. How many dice does she have to glue together?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, one can see many cubes of the same size connected end to end, arranged into a straight, one-layer-thick long strip; each middle cube is connected only to its left and right neighboring cubes, and the two end cubes each have only one connected face. Reasoning: Let there be n dice in total, and let the number of dots on the i-th glued interface be x_i. The problem requires that the two glued faces have the same number of dots; on an ordinary die, the sum of the numbers of dots on opposite faces is 7. Because the long strip in the figure is straight, the left and right glued faces of each internal die are opposite faces, so the numbers of dots on adjacent interfaces satisfy x_i + x_{i+1} = 7, and the interface numbers must alternate between a and 7-a. The total number of dots on the six faces of each die is 1+2+3+4+5+6=21, so before the n dice are glued, the total number of dots is 21n. Each glued interface hides two faces whose number of dots is x_i, so the total number of visible dots S = 21n - 2∑x_i. If n is odd, then the number of interfaces n-1 is even, and the alternating terms sum in pairs to 7, so ∑x_i = 7(n-1)/2, hence S = 21n - 7(n-1) = 14n + 7. At this time n is odd, so S ≡ 21 (mod 28). If n is even, then the number of interfaces n-1 is odd. Let the extra interface number be a, where a∈{1,2,3,4,5,6}; one obtains S = 14(n+1) - 2a. Because n is even, 14(n+1) ≡ 14 (mod 28), so the possible remainders of S are 14-2a, namely 12,10,8,6,4,2 mod 28. The target 2012 has remainder 24 when divided by 28. The remainder 24 is neither 21 in the odd n case, nor among 2,4,6,8,10,12 in the even n case, so 2012 cannot be reached.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a straight one-cube-thick row of dice, so each interior die is glued to its left and right neighbors on opposite faces, while the two end dice have only one glued face. Let the value on the i-th glued interface be x_i. From the text, the two dice at an interface must show equal values on the glued faces, and on an ordinary die opposite faces sum to 7. Therefore for every interior die, x_i+x_{i+1}=7, so the interface values alternate between a and 7-a. The total pips on all dice before hiding glued faces is 21n. Each glued interface hides two faces of value x_i, so the visible total is S=21n-2 sum x_i. If n is odd, the number of interfaces is even and their sum is 7(n-1)/2, giving S=14n+7. If n is even, the number of interfaces is odd and S=14(n+1)-2a for some a in {1,...,6}. Convert these to residues modulo 28: odd n gives 21 mod 28, even n gives one of 2,4,6,8,10,12 mod 28. Since 2012 is 24 mod 28, no case works, so the requested dicebar is impossible.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a dicebar that can be built by attaching cubes one at a time to the exposed end of a straight row. Track the visible-sum change dynamically. For one isolated die the visible sum is 21. Suppose the current exposed end face has value y and Renate glues on a new die with matching value y. The old end face and the new glued face become hidden, and the new die contributes its other five faces, so the net change is 21-2y. On the newly attached die, the next exposed end face has value 7-y because opposite faces of an ordinary die sum to 7. Therefore adding the next die after that changes the sum by 21-2(7-y), and every pair of newly added dice increases the visible total by exactly 28. Thus all odd-length bars have visible sum 21 mod 28. For a two-dice starting bar with glued value a, the visible sum is 42-2a, giving residues 12,10,8,6,4,2 mod 28; adding further pairs preserves those residues. Since 2012 mod 28 is 24, it is not in either the odd-length or even-length residue set, so no number of dice can achieve 2012.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中显示的是一条由许多相同小立方体首尾相接排成的直条状结构，也就是题目中的 dicebar。图中没有显示骰子的点数，只显示这些骰子被排成一条直线，因此可把它理解为每次把一个新骰子粘到当前直条的外露末端。

推理：一个普通骰子六个面的点数总和为 1+2+3+4+5+6=21。单独一个骰子时，所有面都未被粘住，所以非粘合面的点数和为 21。

设当前 dicebar 末端外露面的点数为 y。若粘上一个新骰子，必须用点数同为 y 的面来粘合。这样原来末端的 y 点面和新骰子的 y 点面都会变成粘合面，不再计入；新骰子其余五个面贡献 21-y 点。因此总和的净增加为 (21-y)-y=21-2y。

由于普通骰子相对两面的点数和为 7，新粘上骰子的另一端外露面点数就是 7-y。再粘下一个骰子时，总和的净增加为 21-2(7-y)。所以连续添加两个骰子的总增加量为 (21-2y)+(21-2(7-y))=28。

因此，若骰子数为奇数，从一个骰子的 21 开始，每增加两个骰子，总和增加 28，所以所有奇数长度的 dicebar 的非粘合面点数和都同余于 21 mod 28。

若骰子数为偶数，先看两个骰子的情况。若它们粘合面的点数为 a，则非粘合面点数和为 42-2a，其中 a 可以是 1 到 6。所以可能值模 28 分别为 40,38,36,34,32,30，即 12,10,8,6,4,2 mod 28。之后每增加两个骰子仍增加 28，所以偶数长度只可能属于这些余数。

现在 2012 除以 28，28×71=1988，余数为 24。24 既不是奇数长度可能的余数 21，也不在偶数长度可能的余数集合 {12,10,8,6,4,2} 中。因此无法得到非粘合面点数和正好为 2012。

solver_metadata.cot_raw:
图像描述：图中显示的是一条由许多相同小立方体首尾相接排成的直条状结构，也就是题目中的 dicebar。图中没有显示骰子的点数，只显示这些骰子被排成一条直线，因此可把它理解为每次把一个新骰子粘到当前直条的外露末端。

推理：一个普通骰子六个面的点数总和为 1+2+3+4+5+6=21。单独一个骰子时，所有面都未被粘住，所以非粘合面的点数和为 21。

设当前 dicebar 末端外露面的点数为 y。若粘上一个新骰子，必须用点数同为 y 的面来粘合。这样原来末端的 y 点面和新骰子的 y 点面都会变成粘合面，不再计入；新骰子其余五个面贡献 21-y 点。因此总和的净增加为 (21-y)-y=21-2y。

由于普通骰子相对两面的点数和为 7，新粘上骰子的另一端外露面点数就是 7-y。再粘下一个骰子时，总和的净增加为 21-2(7-y)。所以连续添加两个骰子的总增加量为 (21-2y)+(21-2(7-y))=28。

因此，若骰子数为奇数，从一个骰子的 21 开始，每增加两个骰子，总和增加 28，所以所有奇数长度的 dicebar 的非粘合面点数和都同余于 21 mod 28。

若骰子数为偶数，先看两个骰子的情况。若它们粘合面的点数为 a，则非粘合面点数和为 42-2a，其中 a 可以是 1 到 6。所以可能值模 28 分别为 40,38,36,34,32,30，即 12,10,8,6,4,2 mod 28。之后每增加两个骰子仍增加 28，所以偶数长度只可能属于这些余数。

现在 2012 除以 28，28×71=1988，余数为 24。24 既不是奇数长度可能的余数 21，也不在偶数长度可能的余数集合 {12,10,8,6,4,2} 中。因此无法得到非粘合面点数和正好为 2012。
solver_metadata.model_answer: It is impossible to obtain exactly 2012 points on the non-glued sides, so there is no number of dice Renate can glue together.

raw_record.original_question: Renate wants to glue together a number of ordinary dice (whose number of points on opposite sides always adds up to 7) to form a "dicebar" as shown. She only wants to glue sides together with an equal number of points. She wants the sum of all points on the non-glued sides to equal 2012. How many dice does she have to glue together?
raw_record.answer: It is impossible to obtain exactly 2012 points on the non-glued together sides.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, one can see many cubes of the same size connected end to end, arranged into a straight, one-layer-thick long strip; each middle cube is connected only to its left and right neighboring cubes, and the two end cubes each have only one connected face. Reasoning: Let there be n dice in total, and let the number of dots on the i-th glued interface be x_i. The problem requires that the two glued faces have the same number of dots; on an ordinary die, the sum of the numbers of dots on opposite faces is 7. Because the long strip in the figure is straight, the left and right glued faces of each internal die are opposite faces, so the numbers of dots on adjacent interfaces satisfy x_i + x_{i+1} = 7, and the interface numbers must alternate between a and 7-a. The total number of dots on the six faces of each die is 1+2+3+4+5+6=21, so before the n dice are glued, the total number of dots is 21n. Each glued interface hides two faces whose number of dots is x_i, so the total number of visible dots S = 21n - 2∑x_i. If n is odd, then the number of interfaces n-1 is even, and the alternating terms sum in pairs to 7, so ∑x_i = 7(n-1)/2, hence S = 21n - 7(n-1) = 14n + 7. At this time n is odd, so S ≡ 21 (mod 28). If n is even, then the number of interfaces n-1 is odd. Let the extra interface number be a, where a∈{1,2,3,4,5,6}; one obtains S = 14(n+1) - 2a. Because n is even, 14(n+1) ≡ 14 (mod 28), so the possible remainders of S are 14-2a, namely 12,10,8,6,4,2 mod 28. The target 2012 has remainder 24 when divided by 28. The remainder 24 is neither 21 in the odd n case, nor among 2,4,6,8,10,12 in the even n case, so 2012 cannot be reached.
